verdict.rationale: Harbor Compliance documents a non-interactive, server-to-server OAuth client-credentials flow and a public OpenAPI spec. The API is built for unattended retries, with Idempotency-Key support and Retry-After/X-RateLimit headers, so scripted headless automation is a first-party capability. However, create, update and delete calls need capabilities Harbor must explicitly grant to the account, and refresh tokens are single-use and expire within 30 days, which limits out-of-the-box CI use. Missing for 10: an official CLI or CI integration docs, write access available without vendor approval, and independent or hands-on corroboration of headless/CI usage.
